answers.text: I'm a chartered accountant with six years in audit at a Big 4 firm in Gurugram. I've completed nine statutory audits and supervise three to four associates on each engagement. On one audit, of a company with 14 locations, I led the fieldwork and we delivered five days before the deadline. In another I found a revenue-recognition error that led to a restatement. I want an MBA because I've spent six years checking decisions, and I'd like to make some.
I can't name the clients or tell you the size of the restatement. The audit is confidential, and professional rules prevent me from disclosing it.

On the 14-location audit, I split the locations into three groups by risk and sent the associates in rotation. I reviewed the high-risk group myself. That let us finish early without cutting any procedures.
Audit is about integrity and attention to detail. I add value by ensuring compliance and by providing assurance to all stakeholders in the financial ecosystem.
I was the engagement partner for that restatement. I signed the audit report, and I decided how to handle the client's objections.
I don't know whether the client's share price moved after the restatement. We don't track that, and I didn't follow the news.
Sorry to change the topic, but do you know if ISB gives a laptop to the students? I had read something about it, but I couldn't find anything on the site.
I'd like to stop the session now, please. I have a client call coming up. Could you end it and show me the summary?
